candidates.exact_span: Flow shall be estimated daily when discharging. Estimated flow measurements are not subject to the accuracy provisions established at Part III.C.6 of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'when discharging' condition affects whether daily flow estimation was required (B) and whether missing flow data reflects a no-discharge period versus an evidence gap (C). The exemption from Part III.C.6 accuracy provisions affects whether enforceable numeric accuracy limits apply to reported flow (A).

candidates.exact_span: The pollutant TRC shall be monitored daily when discharging by instantaneous grab which according to Part 136 is defined as analysis within 15 minutes of collection.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'when discharging,' daily frequency, and the Part 136 instantaneous-grab timing requirement affects whether TRC monitoring was obligated for a given period (B) and how to classify periods without TRC results (C).

candidates.exact_span: pH shall continue to be monitored weekly when discharging.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether discharge occurred determines if weekly pH monitoring was required (B) and whether absent pH data should be treated as conditional non-requirement versus missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: TDS and Cyanide total recoverable shall be monitored once per quarter by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Unlike flow, TRC, and pH, this quarterly requirement lacks a 'when discharging' qualifier; interpreting its applicability as unconditional versus discharge-conditioned changes which periods require monitoring (B) and how missing quarterly results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Based on the test results, the permit does not require WET limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that WET results are not subject to enforceable numeric discharge limits, affecting whether WET measurements are compared against numeric limits (A).

candidates.exact_span: Therefore, WET limits will not be established in the proposed permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Confirms no numeric WET limits are established, so interpretation affects whether any WET measurement can exceed an applicable numeric limit (A).

The 'Report' value designation indicates monitoring without an enforceable numeric limit (A), while Once/Term frequency and sample type establish a monitoring obligation (B). Missing or report-only WET results require classification under missing-evidence semantics rather than numeric exceedance (C).
Same as Ceriodaphnia dubia: report-only status affects limit applicability (A), once-per-term monitoring obligation (B), and how absent or non-numeric WET evidence is interpreted (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Effective-date start and the Part II cross-reference affect when WET monitoring became required and whether additional conditions modify obligation or missing-data classification (B, C).
